slides.title: prompts to learn any language with AI
slides.voiceover: Here are six prompts to learn any language with ChatGPT or Claude.

slides.name: The Placement Test
slides.sub: Find your real level in two minutes, no guessing.
slides.prompt: I want to learn [LANGUAGE]. Ask me 8 short questions in [LANGUAGE], mixed from easy to hard, to test my vocabulary and grammar. After my answers, tell me my level on the CEFR scale (A1-C2) and the 3 things I should work on first.
slides.voiceover: One. A quick quiz that tells you your real level, not a guess.

slides.name: The Conversation Partner
slides.sub: A 5-minute role-play in your target language, every day.
slides.prompt: Be my conversation partner in [LANGUAGE] at a [YOUR LEVEL] level. Play the role of [SCENARIO, e.g. a barista in Paris]. Reply only in [LANGUAGE], keep it short, and gently correct my grammar in [YOUR LANGUAGE] after each of my turns.
slides.tip: Do this for 5 minutes a day instead of one long session a week — it sticks better.
slides.voiceover: Two. A daily role-play partner that corrects you as you go.

slides.name: The Mistake Corrector
slides.sub: Turn your own sentences into a mini grammar lesson.
slides.prompt: Here is a paragraph I wrote in [LANGUAGE]: [PASTE TEXT]. Correct every mistake, show the original next to the fix, explain the grammar rule behind each correction in [YOUR LANGUAGE], and rate my writing from 1 to 10.

lines: Rule: past tense needs the past participle

slides.voiceover: Three. Paste anything you wrote, get a real grammar breakdown.

slides.name: The Pronunciation Coach
slides.sub: Phonetic breakdowns for the words that trip you up.
slides.prompt: Break down how to pronounce this [LANGUAGE] word or phrase: [WORD]. Give me a phonetic spelling I can actually read, which syllable to stress, one similar-sounding English word, and a common mistake learners make with it.
slides.tip: If your app has a voice conversation feature, say the word out loud afterward and ask how it sounded.
slides.voiceover: Four. Get a phonetic spelling for any word that trips you up.

slides.name: The Flashcard Generator
slides.sub: Turn any text into a ready-to-study vocabulary set.
slides.prompt: Read this [LANGUAGE] text: [PASTE TEXT]. Pick the 10 most useful words or phrases for a [YOUR LEVEL] learner. For each one, give the translation, one example sentence, and a memory trick. Format it as a simple flashcard list.
slides.voiceover: Five. Any article becomes a ten-card vocabulary deck.

slides.name: The Culture Guide
slides.sub: The context a textbook always skips.
slides.prompt: Explain the cultural context behind this [LANGUAGE] expression or custom: [TOPIC]. When would a native speaker actually use it, is it formal or casual, and is there anything a foreigner should avoid saying or doing around it?
slides.voiceover: Six. The cultural context your textbook never explains.

slides.title: Get more out of this pack
items: Stick with it for a full week before you switch.
Turn your corrected sentences into your own flashcard deck.
Five minutes with the conversation partner beats one hour, once a week.
slides.voiceover: Pick one language, save your corrections, and use it daily.
